## The model

The package implements the methods of Qu and Perron (2007) for a system of
$n$ equations observed over $T$ periods with $m$ breaks at unknown dates
$T_1 < \dots < T_m$:

$$y_t = (I_n \otimes z_t') S \beta_j + u_t, \qquad E[u_t u_t'] = \Sigma_j, \qquad t = T_{j-1} + 1, \dots, T_j,$$

where $z_t$ holds every regressor of the system, $S$ selects which regressors
enter which equation, $\beta_j$ are the coefficients of regime $j$ and
$\Sigma_j$ its error covariance matrix. The breaks may affect the
coefficients, the covariance matrix, or both, and coefficients can be held
fixed across regimes. The package provides

* quasi-maximum-likelihood estimates of the break dates and coefficients;
* the sup-LR test against a fixed number of breaks, the double-maximum tests
  UDmax and WDmax, and the sequential test Seq($\ell+1|\ell$), with critical
  values for any number of changing parameters;
* confidence intervals for the break dates;
* the locally ordered breaks model of Section 5 of the paper;
* simulation functions for Monte Carlo work.

The user never builds $S$ or restriction matrices by hand: one function per
model type does it. We use the two data sets distributed with the original
GAUSS code throughout.

```{r}
library(mvbreak)
y <- as.matrix(data1[, 1:2])      # two dependent variables
z <- as.matrix(data1[, 3:5])      # a constant and two regressors
```

## Seemingly unrelated regressions

In the example of the original code, equation 1 uses the first regressor and
equation 2 the second, both with an intercept, and two breaks are allowed in
every coefficient. `breaks_sur()` takes a list with the regressors of each
equation; `m` is the number of breaks estimated and `trim` the minimum length
of a regime as a fraction of the sample.

```{r}
fit <- breaks_sur(y, x = list(z[, 2, drop = FALSE], z[, 3, drop = FALSE]), m = 2, trim = 0.2)
fit
```

The break dates 56 and 100 and the coefficients reproduce the output of the
GAUSS program. `summary()` adds standard errors, and the usual methods are
available.

```{r}
summary(fit)
coef(fit)
logLik(fit)
```

### Tests for the number of breaks

`test_breaks()` computes every test for the fitted model: the sup-LR test of
no break against 1, ..., `max_breaks` breaks, the double-maximum tests
against an unknown number of breaks up to `max_breaks`, and the sequential
tests. Critical values come from a table simulated for up to 60 changing
parameters per break; cases outside it are simulated on the fly.

```{r}
test_breaks(fit)
```

`select_breaks()` applies the procedure recommended in the paper: a
double-maximum test decides whether there is at least one break, and the
sequential test then adds breaks one at a time. The model is refitted with the
number of breaks chosen.

```{r}
fit3 <- breaks_sur(y, x = list(z[, 2, drop = FALSE], z[, 3, drop = FALSE]), m = 3, trim = 0.2)
chosen <- suppressWarnings(select_breaks(fit3, max_breaks = 3))
chosen$n_breaks
chosen$fit$dates
```

(The warning suppressed here says that no segment of the two-break partition
is long enough to hold a third break with this trimming, so Seq(3|2) is `NA`.)

### Confidence intervals for the break dates

`confint_breaks()` gives the intervals of Theorem 3 of the paper. `robust = TRUE`
allows serially correlated errors through a HAC estimate, `prewhit = TRUE`
prewhitens it, and `hetq = TRUE` lets the regressors' distribution differ across
regimes. The `plot()` method shades them.

```{r}
ci <- confint_breaks(fit, level = c(0.90, 0.95))
ci
plot(fit, ci = ci)
```

### Partial structural change

Coefficients can be held fixed across regimes by name. Here the slopes are
constant and only the intercepts change, which is the restricted model of the
original example (dates 50 and 99).

```{r}
fit_r <- breaks_sur(y, x = list(z[, 2, drop = FALSE], z[, 3, drop = FALSE]), m = 2, trim = 0.2,
                    fixed = c("y1:x1", "y2:x1"))
fit_r$dates
test_breaks(fit_r, tests = "supLR")
```

## A VAR

`breaks_varp()` builds the lags itself. `change` says what the breaks affect:
the coefficients (`"coef"`, the default), the covariance matrix of the errors
(`"cov"`), or both. With serially correlated errors, `robust = TRUE` replaces
the sup-LR by a HAC-based sup-F test for the coefficients.

```{r}
var_fit <- breaks_varp(y, p = 1, m = 1, trim = 0.2, change = "both")
var_fit$dates
test_breaks(var_fit)
```

Whole equations can be held fixed with `fixed_equations`, for example when only
the first equation is allowed to change.

```{r}
breaks_varp(y, p = 1, m = 1, trim = 0.2, fixed_equations = "y2")$dates
```

## Other model types

* `breaks_mvreg(y, x)` fits a multivariate regression with the same regressors
  in every equation; with `x = NULL` it is a model of means and covariance.
* `breaks_panel(y, x)` fits a panel with unit-specific intercepts, pooled
  slopes and breaks common to all units.
* `breaks_system(y, z, S)` is the general entry point, where the selection
  matrix $S$ and, if needed, the restriction matrix $R$ are supplied directly.

```{r}
breaks_mvreg(y, x = NULL, m = 1, trim = 0.2, change = "both")$dates
```

## Critical values

`critical_values()` returns the critical values used by the tests for a given
number of changing parameters `q`, number of breaks and trimming. Bai and
Perron's response surfaces stop at `q = 10`; the shipped table goes to
`q = 60`, and anything beyond is simulated.

```{r}
critical_values(q = 4, m = 2, trm = 0.2)
```

## Locally ordered breaks

When the breaks of two groups of equations are close to each other, the
common-break model is misspecified and treating the equations separately
loses efficiency. `breaks_ordered()` estimates the two dates jointly, with the
equations in `first` breaking first. The LR test of no break uses the pairs
whose distance is at most `max_gap`, and the intervals of Theorem 4 are
simulated.

```{r}
y2 <- as.matrix(data2[, 1:2]); z2 <- as.matrix(data2[, 3:5])
ord <- breaks_ordered(y2, x = list(z2[, 2, drop = FALSE], z2[, 3, drop = FALSE]), trim = 0.2)
ord
test_breaks(ord)
confint_breaks(ord, seed = 1)
```

## Simulation

Every model type has a generator for Monte Carlo work. The object returned
carries the true dates and coefficients in the layout of the fitted model.

```{r}
A1 <- rbind(c(0.5, 0.1), c(0.0, 0.3)); A2 <- rbind(c(-0.2, 0.0), c(0.2, 0.6))
sim <- simulate_varp(200, coef = list(cbind(0, A1), cbind(1, A2)), sigma = diag(2), dates = 100, seed = 1)
sim
fit_sim <- breaks_varp(sim$y, p = 1, m = 1)
fit_sim$dates
cbind(true = sim$dgp$coef_matrix[, 2], estimated = coef(fit_sim)[, 2])
```

## References

Bai, J. and P. Perron (1998), "Estimating and Testing Linear Models with
Multiple Structural Changes", *Econometrica*, 66, 47–78.

Qu, Z. and P. Perron (2007), "Estimating and Testing Structural Changes in
Multivariate Regressions", *Econometrica*, 75, 459–502.
